notes: Snapshot of sources verified while building the CampSitesUSA catalog. Counts are what the endpoints returned on 2026-11-15 and will drift. 'redistributable' is a practical guide, not legal advice: yes = public domain/open license; attr = attribution required; check = read the operator's terms before storing or republishing; no = do not scrape or redistribute, deep-link instead.

sources.name: National Park Service Data API
sources.coverage: 475 park units; 665 campgrounds; alerts, things to do, visitor centers, webcams, passport stamps
sources.auth: Free API key; DEMO_KEY works for testing at low rate
sources.update: Alerts about every 2 hours; park content periodically
sources.notes: Best free source for park boundaries, official campgrounds, fees, alerts and activities. Campground payload includes site counts, amenities, RV max length and reservation links.

sources.name: Recreation Information Database (RIDB)
sources.coverage: 12 federal agencies: rec areas, facilities, campsites, activities, media
sources.notes: The supported federal recreation API. Covers NPS, USFS, BLM, USACE, BOR, FWS and others. Does NOT include live availability; availability is separate and behind recreation.gov.

sources.name: Recreation.gov public search API (unofficial)
sources.coverage: 7,549 camping-related listings and 4,523 campgrounds at snapshot; includes NPS, USFS, BLM, USACE, BOR, FWS and state partners
sources.license: Public listing data; API is undocumented and subject to Recreation.gov terms
sources.notes: Richest single national campground inventory found: capacity, equipment, RV length, price range, ratings, cell coverage. Treat as a cacheable snapshot, not a supported API. Do not poll availability endpoints.

sources.name: Recreation.gov availability endpoints (undocumented)
sources.coverage: Per-campground monthly site availability
sources.license: Recreation.gov terms; not a public API
sources.notes: Works but unsupported and can change or block without notice. For a product, use Campflare or another partner API, or deep-link to recreation.gov.

sources.name: USFS Recreation Opportunities (EDW)
sources.coverage: 14,211 recreation opportunity points nationwide (campgrounds, cabins, trailheads, OHV, etc.)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 / public domain per data.gov listing
sources.notes: Filter markeractivitygroup = 'Camping & Cabins' for campgrounds; also useful for trailheads, OHV and horse camps. Descriptions carry fee and restriction text.

sources.name: USFS National Forest System Trails (EDW)
sources.coverage: National Forest System trails with trail class, surface, allowed uses
sources.notes: Trail Class 1-5 is a ready-made difficulty grade. Pair with USGS 3DEP for elevation gain.

sources.name: USFS Motor Vehicle Use Maps (MVUM)
sources.coverage: Roads and trails designated for motor vehicle use, nationwide
sources.notes: The legal basis for dispersed camping along forest roads. The symbology distinguishes roads open to all vehicles, high-clearance, and trails. Essential for a 'can I camp here?' answer.

sources.name: BLM National Recreation Sites & Facilities
sources.coverage: 1,269 facilities/sites; 539 RIDB camping points
sources.notes: Layer 2 is the camping layer and includes stay limits and fee text. There is still no nationwide BLM dispersed-camping polygon layer; use PAD-US BLM ownership + MVUM-equivalent local rules.

sources.name: Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US 4.1)
sources.coverage: Fee ownership and management of every public parcel plus conservation easements
sources.access: ArcGIS REST / GeoPackage / Shapefile / File Geodatabase
sources.notes: The single most useful layer for answering 'whose land is this?'. Convert to PMTiles for offline use.

sources.name: BLM National Surface Management Agency
sources.coverage: Surface management agency polygons for the western US
sources.notes: Finer-grained than PAD-US in BLM country; good cross-check for ownership boundaries.

sources.name: US Army Corps of Engineers recreation areas
sources.coverage: Lake and river project campgrounds, day-use areas, boat ramps
sources.notes: No single national USACE campground API, but USACE facilities are well represented in Recreation.gov/RIDB. Some districts publish their own GIS.

sources.name: US Fish & Wildlife Service refuges
sources.coverage: National Wildlife Refuge System units, trails, hunting/fishing access
sources.access: ArcGIS services / refuge pages; Recreation.gov for some campgrounds
sources.notes: Camping rules vary by refuge and are often primitive or prohibited. Treat as an activity/hunting layer more than a camping layer.

sources.name: Bureau of Reclamation recreation
sources.coverage: Reclamation reservoirs and recreation areas, mostly western states
sources.notes: Many Reclamation campgrounds are concession-operated and listed on Recreation.gov.

sources.name: Tennessee Valley Authority recreation
sources.coverage: TVA reservoirs, campgrounds, day-use areas in TN, AL, GA, KY, NC, VA, MS
sources.notes: TVA campgrounds are often free or cheap and poorly covered elsewhere. Manual curation required.

sources.name: Military MWR campgrounds
sources.coverage: On-base and recreation-area campgrounds for eligible users
sources.auth: None for directory; eligibility required to stay
sources.license: Directory is third-party; base pages are public info
sources.notes: Useful niche inventory for veterans/active duty. Verify eligibility and access rules.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap
sources.coverage: Worldwide; campsites, dump stations, water, showers, rest areas, trails, landuse
sources.auth: None (be polite; use a real User-Agent)
sources.notes: Best open source of informal/free sites. ODbL share-alike means derived databases need careful handling. Great for amenities too.

sources.name: Freecampsites.net
sources.coverage: Tens of thousands of user-submitted free/cheap campsites, dump stations and reviews across the US
sources.access: Website + internal JSON endpoint used by its map
sources.update: Continuous user submissions; listings go stale
sources.notes: See docs/FREECAMPSITES.md. Do not scrape or republish bulk data without permission; deep-link to listings and use it as a research/reference layer.

sources.name: iOverlander
sources.coverage: Worldwide community database of overnight spots, informal camps, water, dump, propane, mechanics
sources.license: Community-contributed; no open data license published
sources.notes: Strongest coverage for remote international/overland spots. Closed data; use links or seek a partnership.

sources.name: Campendium
sources.coverage: Public and private campgrounds, free sites, dump stations, cell signal reports
sources.notes: Best community cell-signal and free-site reviews. Closed; deep-link only.

sources.name: The Dyrt
sources.coverage: Public/private campgrounds, dispersed sites, reviews, photos, availability
sources.notes: Large review corpus. Partnership required for data use.

sources.name: Hipcamp
sources.coverage: Private land camping: farms, ranches, vineyards, glamping
sources.notes: Dominant private-land marketplace. Third-party scrapers exist but violate terms.

sources.name: AllStays
sources.coverage: RV parks, campgrounds, free overnight spots, rest areas, dump stations, Walmarts, truck stops
sources.notes: The most comprehensive overnight-stop directory for RVers. Closed.

sources.name: RV Parky
sources.coverage: RV parks, campgrounds, free overnight locations, dump stations
sources.notes: Free directory with user reviews; useful cross-check for Walmart/truck-stop overnighting.

sources.name: OvernightRVParking.com
sources.coverage: Verified free overnight parking locations (Walmart, Cracker Barrel, casinos, truck stops)
sources.notes: Policies change frequently; always call ahead. Closed data.

sources.name: Harvest Hosts / Boondockers Welcome
sources.coverage: Member-only stays at farms, wineries, museums, businesses and private hosts
sources.notes: Membership inventory, not publicly listable. Integration only via partnership.

sources.name: KOA
sources.coverage: ~500 franchised campgrounds in the US and Canada
sources.notes: Franchise network with reliable amenity standards; no public API.

sources.name: Good Sam
sources.coverage: RV parks and campgrounds with ratings; discount network
sources.notes: Park ratings and trip planning; closed.

sources.name: Thousand Trails
sources.coverage: Membership campground network
sources.notes: Membership-only; not a general inventory source.

sources.name: Passport America
sources.coverage: Discount RV parks (50% off)
sources.notes: Discount network; useful price signal, not a campsite database.

sources.name: Escapees RV Club
sources.coverage: Member parks, co-ops, mail service, boondocking community
sources.notes: Long-term boondocker community and membership parks.

sources.name: Campflare API
sources.coverage: Recreation.gov campground availability and alerts
sources.notes: Practical, supported way to get availability/cancellations without scraping Recreation.gov.

sources.name: ReserveAmerica (Aspira)
sources.coverage: State park and private campground reservations in many states
sources.notes: Largest state-park booking platform. No public API; deep-link to state-branded search pages.

sources.name: ReserveCalifornia
sources.coverage: California state park campsites and lodging
sources.notes: California-only system; not on ReserveAmerica.

sources.name: GoingToCamp
sources.coverage: Washington State Parks and other public land agencies
sources.notes: Used by WA and some Canadian agencies.

sources.name: US eDirect
sources.coverage: Arizona, Minnesota and other state park reservation systems
sources.notes: White-label reservation platform; state-specific storefronts.

sources.name: 50 state park systems
sources.coverage: 50 state park systems, thousands of campgrounds
sources.access: Websites; reservation platforms vary by state
sources.license: Varies by state; most park info is public record
sources.notes: No national state-park API. Build per-state adapters or link out. Table in docs/STATE-PARKS.md.

sources.name: National Weather Service API
sources.coverage: US forecasts, hourly/daily, alerts, gridpoints
sources.notes: Free and reliable. Great for overnight lows, wind and alerts. Cache gridpoint forecasts.

sources.name: Open-Meteo
sources.coverage: Global forecast, historical weather, air quality, elevation
sources.auth: None for non-commercial; paid for high volume
sources.notes: Good fallback/global option. Useful for trip planning beyond the US too.

sources.name: NIFC WFIGS wildfire perimeters and incidents
sources.coverage: Active wildfire perimeters, incidents, public notices
sources.notes: Show fire distance and closures near a site. Pair with agency fire restrictions.

sources.name: AirNow
sources.coverage: AQI and pollutant observations/forecasts
sources.notes: Essential for smoke-season camping. Also see AirNow's public GIS files.

sources.name: NOAA Hazard Mapping System smoke
sources.coverage: Satellite-derived smoke plumes over North America
sources.notes: Complements AQI with a visual smoke plume layer.

sources.name: FCC National Broadband Map (mobile)
sources.coverage: Carrier-reported mobile coverage (4G/5G) by technology and provider
sources.notes: Carrier-reported coverage is optimistic; use as a hint, not a promise. Community signal reports (Campendium) are often more honest.

sources.name: VIIRS Nighttime Lights / light pollution
sources.coverage: Global nighttime radiance composites
sources.notes: Derive a dark-sky score per campsite. Pair with NPS night-sky data.

sources.name: USGS 3DEP Elevation
sources.coverage: National elevation (DEM), 1/3 to 1 m in many areas
sources.notes: Elevation at camp, road grade, trail gain, and a proxy for colder overnight lows.

sources.name: USGS National Water Information System
sources.coverage: Streamflow, gauge height, water temperature, water quality
sources.notes: Answer 'is the river runnable/fishable today?' for paddling and fishing sites.

sources.name: NOAA Tides & Currents
sources.coverage: Tide predictions, currents, water levels, met observations
sources.notes: Important for coastal campsites, clam digging, kayaking and beach driving.

sources.name: NRCS SNOTEL / snowpack
sources.coverage: Mountain snow depth, SWE, temperature at remote stations
sources.notes: Answers 'is the high-country road or camp accessible?' in shoulder seasons.

sources.name: State 511 road condition systems
sources.coverage: Closures, chain controls, construction, cameras (state by state)
sources.notes: No national 511 API. Build adapters for the states you cover; FHWA has a 511 directory.

sources.name: Wikidata / Wikipedia
sources.coverage: Parks, protected areas, campgrounds, trailheads, elevation, photos, IDs
sources.notes: Excellent for enriching parks with descriptions, photos and cross-IDs. Check individual photo licenses.

sources.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS)
sources.coverage: Official names and coordinates for US geographic features
sources.notes: Normalize place names and find springs, gaps, trailheads and historic sites.

sources.name: Census TIGER/Line
sources.coverage: State, county, place, tribal, road and boundary files
sources.notes: Counties, states and tribal areas for filtering and offline packs.

sources.name: USGS National Digital Trails
sources.coverage: National trails dataset assembled from federal and state sources
sources.notes: Good national baseline; verify local accuracy. Pair with USFS trails and OSM.

sources.name: American Whitewater
sources.coverage: Whitewater rivers, reaches, rapids, flow recommendations, gauges
sources.notes: Best whitewater difficulty/flow cross-reference for paddling campers.

sources.name: State fish & wildlife agencies
sources.coverage: Fishing access, stocking, hunting seasons, WMA camping rules, licenses
sources.notes: The only reliable source for WMA camping legality and hunting-season closures.

sources.name: NPS alerts, closures and conditions
sources.coverage: Park alerts, closures, fire restrictions, road status
sources.notes: Must-have for any site inside or adjacent to an NPS unit.

sources.name: RIDB activities and facilities
sources.coverage: Activity taxonomy and facility-activity links across federal agencies
sources.notes: Canonical activity vocabulary for filtering (hiking, boating, OHV, fishing, etc.).

sources.name: USFS fire restrictions
sources.coverage: Forest-by-forest fire restrictions and closures
sources.access: Web pages / news releases / some ArcGIS
sources.notes: No single national feed; aggregate per forest or via regional news releases.

sources.name: BLM fire restrictions
sources.coverage: State/district fire restrictions and temporary closures
sources.notes: Check the state office page; restrictions are often issued at district level.

sources.name: OSM amenities for campers
sources.coverage: Dump stations, drinking water, showers, laundromats, propane, fuel, rest areas, groceries
sources.notes: The best open layer for 'services along the way'. Verify hours/seasonality with reviews.

sources.name: Sanidumps
sources.coverage: RV dump stations in the US and Canada
sources.notes: Cross-check OSM dump stations; closed data.

sources.name: State rest areas
sources.coverage: Rest areas, welcome centers, truck parking, some overnight-allowed
sources.notes: Overnight rules differ by state and site; never assume. OSM is the best open base layer.

sources.name: Protomaps / OpenStreetMap basemaps
sources.coverage: Global vector basemap as PMTiles, self-hostable
sources.auth: None for self-hosted builds; paid CDN optional
sources.notes: Makes offline region packs realistic: one PMTiles file per state or region.

sources.name: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer
sources.coverage: Flood zones and floodways
sources.notes: Useful for riverside campsite risk, especially in monsoon season.

sources.name: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
sources.coverage: Aurora forecast, Kp index, space weather alerts
sources.notes: Aurora-chasing campers care about this; combine with dark-sky score and cloud forecast.

sources.name: NPS night sky / dark sky places
sources.coverage: International Dark Sky Places, NPS night-sky programs
sources.notes: Enrich stargazing sites; pair with VIIRS radiance.

sources.name: BIA / Census tribal areas
sources.coverage: American Indian reservations, trust lands, Alaska Native village areas
sources.notes: Critical guardrail: tribal land is not public land. Show 'permission required' and never route users to camp there without explicit authorization.

sources.name: State trust lands
sources.coverage: Arizona, New Mexico, Utah, Colorado, Texas and others
sources.notes: A common trap: trust land looks public but is often closed or permit-only. Arizona requires a recreation permit. Encode state-specific rules.

sources.name: County, city and regional parks
sources.coverage: Tens of thousands of local parks, many with cheap or free camping
sources.license: ODbL for OSM; local data varies
sources.notes: The long tail. OSM is the only practical national base; add first-party reports for the best local spots.

sources.name: Utility company campgrounds
sources.operator: TVA, SCE, PG&E, APS, SRP and others
sources.coverage: Cheap or free campgrounds near reservoirs and utility land, mostly Southeast and West
sources.notes: Underrated and poorly aggregated. Good differentiation for a Southeast launch.

sources.name: Casino overnight parking
sources.coverage: Casino lots that allow RV overnighting, mostly in the West and South
sources.notes: Policies change often. Always advise calling the casino. Link out to directories rather than ingesting.

sources.name: Truck stop overnighting
sources.coverage: Thousands of truck stops with RV parking, showers, dump stations, propane
sources.notes: A reliable fallback for a night on the road. Show brand, amenities and 'call ahead' guidance.

sources.name: Walmart / Cracker Barrel overnight policies
sources.coverage: Store lots that permit overnight RV parking where local law allows
sources.notes: Corporate policy defers to the store and local law. Never present as guaranteed. Deep-link to store finder and advise calling.

sources.name: BLM Long Term Visitor Areas (LTVA)
sources.coverage: Winter LTVA sites in Arizona and California (Quartzsite, Yuma, Imperial Dam, etc.)
sources.auth: None for info; permit required to stay
sources.notes: A key snowbird product. Season permits are roughly $180 and include water/dump/trash at some areas. Verify current fees.

sources.name: National Wild and Scenic Rivers
sources.coverage: Wild and Scenic River segments and classifications
sources.notes: Enrich paddling, fishing and scenic-camp recommendations; also a proxy for protected corridors.

sources.name: National Trails System
sources.coverage: National Scenic, Historic and Recreation Trails
sources.notes: Long-distance routes (AT, PCT, CDT, etc.) with camping and resupply context.

sources.name: eBird
sources.coverage: Bird sightings, hotspots, species by location/season
sources.license: eBird terms; observation data has attribution requirements
sources.notes: Great for wildlife/birding campers. Use hotspots and recent sightings, not bulk observation dumps.

sources.name: iNaturalist
sources.operator: California Academy of Sciences / National Geographic
sources.coverage: Wildlife, plant and fungi observations worldwide
sources.auth: None for read; account for write
sources.license: CC BY-NC / CC BY / CC0 per observation
sources.notes: Seasonal wildlife highlights near camp. Respect per-observation licenses and obscure sensitive locations.

sources.name: Recreation.gov permits and lotteries
sources.coverage: Wilderness permits, river permits, lotteries, timed entry
sources.auth: None for search; account to apply
sources.notes: Explains why a campground may look 'closed': access may require a separate permit or lottery.
